title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
claim: Ln3+ luminescence is fixed mainly by the first coordination shell, but ion–ion interactions in extended solids can partially quench emission and change lifetimes, so dimensionality can affect optics even when slow relaxation remains single-ion.
explanation: The magneto-optical analysis has been extended to a 1D cyano-bridged chain and 2D phosphonate polymers with Dy3+ single-ion relaxation and no spin-carrier interaction required for the magnetism. The authors still flag possible optical quenching by ion–ion coupling and say systematic dimensionality comparisons remain to be done.
scope: Extended Dy3+ coordination polymers that show single-ion slow relaxation and Ln luminescence.
conditions: Systems in which magnetic relaxation is of single-ion origin.
caveats: The influence of dimensionality on emission is proposed, not demonstrated by a completed comparative study.
